def: Properties of a model choice that cannot be changed or traded away, such as the licence and where data may go, and so are used to filter candidates first.
Properties of a model choice that can be improved or traded against each other, such as accuracy, latency and cost, compared after the hard attributes have filtered the list.
A requirement that data is stored and processed in a given country or region.
A contractual commitment by a model provider not to keep prompts and outputs beyond processing the request.
A hosted model whose weights the vendor keeps closed, used by sending requests and paying per token.
A model whose trained parameters are published for download, which is not necessarily open source and may carry a custom licence.
A head-to-head run of candidate models on the same gold set, with the same scoring and a comparable prompting budget, to choose between them by evidence.
Storing a model's weights in fewer bits, such as 8 or 4, to cut memory use at some cost in quality that must be re-measured.
